s1.syndrome_frame: Impacted tooth with associated radiographic lesion
salient_findings: Radiopaque lesion in the left mandibular anterior region
key_facts: 22-year-old woman
All permanent teeth erupted except third molars and lower left lateral incisor
Mild spacing between lower left central incisor and canine
Class II, Division 1 malocclusion
Crowding in maxillary anterior region
No history of prior dental extractions
Unerupted lower left lateral incisor with associated radiopaque lesion
Radiopaque lesion surrounded by thin radiolucent halo
Lesion obstructs eruption path of tooth

differentials: Keratocystic odontogenic tumor associated with nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome
per_call: Keratocystic odontogenic tumor associated with nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome

shortlist.label: Compound odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Radiopaque lesion associated with unerupted tooth

shortlist.label: Dentigerous cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Radiolucent halo surrounding radiopaque lesion obstructing tooth eruption

shortlist.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Association with unerupted teeth and radiographic appearance

shortlist.label: Complex odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar radiographic appearance to compound odontoma

shortlist.label: Calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Radiographic appearance and potential to obstruct tooth eruption

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-defined radiopaque lesion surrounded by a thin radiolucent halo, associated with an unerupted tooth, is characteristic of an odontoma, and the compound type is the most common odontogenic tumor that can cause tooth impaction.

rejected.label: Dentigerous cyst
rejected.why: Dentigerous cysts typically appear as a radiolucent lesion surrounding the crown of an unerupted tooth, not a radiopaque lesion.

rejected.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumors often present as a radiolucent lesion with a radiopaque border, not a solid radiopaque lesion.

rejected.label: Complex odontoma
rejected.why: Complex odontomas are typically seen as a radiopaque mass without an obvious association with an unerupted tooth, and are less common than compound odontomas.

rejected.label: Calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: Calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumors are rare and usually present with a mix of radiolucent and radiopaque areas, not a well-defined radiopaque lesion with a thin radiolucent halo.
